article.Citation/Title: D.C. Mash, Kovera, C. A., Pablo, J., Tyndale, R. F., Ervin, F. D., Williams, I. C., Singleton, E. G., & Mayor, M. (2000). Ibogaine: Complex pharmacokinetics, concerns for safety, and preliminary efficacy measures. Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, 914, 394-401.
article.InterventionDescription: Oral ibogaine HCl, single fixed dose (500, 600, or 800 mg), given during a 14-day open-label inpatient detoxification program for opioid- or cocaine-dependent adults.

article.Outcome: No single statistic is designated 'primary' by the authors. The Abstract's first substantive finding sentence is 'ibogaine significantly decreased craving for cocaine and heroin during inpatient detoxification,' with depressive-symptom improvement introduced afterward as 'also' significant -- so per the precedence rule (author designation > abstract-led SUD outcome > largest of co-equal), craving is the SUD-behavioral outcome the abstract leads with, ranking it above the Results section's BDI-first ordering and above depression (not an SUD outcome). Craving itself is reported as 5 subscales x 2 drug groups (10 F-tests, Tables 2-3) with none singled out as primary. Restricting to the opiate-craving subscales (HCQN-29, Table 2) because this record's Condition is 'Opioid', the largest/most significant of the 5 co-equal subscales is Intention to Use, F(3,24)=81.38, p=.0001. Outcome = 3.26 (pre-ibogaine) - 1.57 (post-ibogaine) = 1.69, the pre/post reduction on the 0-6 HCQN-29 scale (Table 2), computed directly from the two reported means (arithmetic only, no assumed model). The parallel cocaine-craving subscales (Table 3) were not selected given the Condition='Opioid' framing; the largest of those is Relief of Negative States, F(2,10)=15.26, p=.0005, noted here in case this choice is revisited.
article.SD: F(3,24) = 81.38, the omnibus repeated-measures ANOVA statistic printed in the same row/table (TABLE 2) as the Intention-to-Use means used for Outcome. Numerator df=3 implies a 4-level within-subjects time factor (matching the Methods' 'three different time points...and at one month following discharge'), with the 1-month point excluded from the table ('data not shown' per Results) but still contributing to the omnibus test.
article.PVal: p = .0001 as printed in TABLE 2, same row as the Intention-to-Use F-statistic and means used for Outcome/SD.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Not reported. The article gives only the total enrolled N (27: 23 men, 4 women) and separate mean ages for the 'opiate group' and 'cocaine group' without stating either subgroup's size. TABLE 2's F(3,24) implies an error df of 24, which is consistent with several different repeated-measures error structures (one-way within-subjects on the opiate subgroup alone vs. a mixed model with drug-of-abuse as a between-subjects factor) that would each imply a different N -- back-calculating N from df would require assuming an ANOVA design the Methods paragraph does not confirm, which is exactly the kind of unstated decoding rule the extraction spec prohibits. Coded '.' rather than inferred.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 12 of 14 criteria are explicitly described. Comparator and randomization are never mentioned in any form anywhere in the article -- no 'control,' 'randomiz-', or comparable language occurs -- so neither is described as present or as absent, and both are coded N (a genuine gap, not an inferred absence). Setting is inferred only from co-author affiliation (e) and the acknowledgments naming the Healing Visions Institute, St. Kitts, W.I., rather than an explicit statement of the treatment site in Methods. Blinding is described via the explicit 'open-label conditions' phrase. Harms is coded Y on the single explicit tolerability sentence ('Ibogaine was well tolerated...') even though it is brief and cites a companion paper for detail. All remaining elements (objective, design, eligibility, intervention, outcomes, sample size, statistics, results, funding) are explicitly and specifically described.

article.RandomizationYN: Coded 0, not '.' or 3. Methods states participants were 'assigned to one of three fixed-dose (500, 600, or 800 mg) ibogaine HCl treatments under open-label conditions' with no mention of a randomization procedure and no other arm to randomize against (every participant received ibogaine). Treated as a single-arm design per the boundary rule (single-arm/open-label studies code 0, not 3), since nothing in the text suggests dose assignment was a randomized comparison rather than a non-comparative dosing schedule.
article.BlindingYN: 0. Methods explicitly states treatment was administered 'under open-label conditions'.
article.Comparator: 0. No control, placebo, or comparison group is mentioned anywhere in the article. The three fixed doses (500/600/800 mg) are not analyzed as a dose-comparison design -- no results are stratified or contrasted by dose; the reported RM-ANOVAs use 'primary drug of abuse (opiates versus cocaine)' as the between-subjects factor, not dose -- so the 'high vs low dose counts as a comparator' provision does not apply here.
article.PrimaryCare: 0. Treatment occurred in an inpatient detoxification/research setting; no interface with primary-care providers or settings is mentioned.
article.Power: 1, a close call. No formal a priori or post hoc power calculation is reported. The Discussion states: 'A limitation of the study is that it is based on findings in only 27 subjects; thus, replication is needed in future studies to determine the stability of the findings.' Treated as functionally equivalent to the 'bare statement that the study was underpowered' provision, since it explicitly frames small sample size as a limitation on the reliability of the findings.
article.Retention (%): Not calculable. The study was not randomized, so the denominator would be the enrolled N (27), but the article never reports how many of the 27 completed the 14-day inpatient program or the 1-month follow-up assessment (the 1-month craving data are described only as 'data not shown'). No completer count is given anywhere in the text.
article.ConfoundYN: 1, on substantive-discussion grounds rather than formal statistical adjustment. Results explicitly checks a candidate confound: CYP2D6 extensive-metabolizer proportions were compared between opioid- and cocaine-dependent groups and found 'not significantly different... (data not shown).' Discussion also attributes the null cocaine Desire-to-Use/Intention-to-Use findings 'in part because of floor effects at pre-ibogaine assessments and because of the small sample size,' a substantive discussion of a moderating factor.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: 1. Methods states subjects 'met inclusion/exclusion criteria' and specifies several: DSM-IV criteria for cocaine or opioid dependence, positive urine screens at entry, no history of stroke/epilepsy/axis I psychotic disorders, and ECG/labs within predetermined limits.
article.BaseStatus: '.' No DSM-5-style severity specifier or count of dependence criteria is reported (study used DSM-IV, which lacks a built-in severity grade), and no ASI composite/severity score is reported in Results despite the ASI having been administered at admission. Inpatient detoxification and clinically significant baseline BDI scores (>=11) suggest substantial severity but do not support a specific Mild/Moderate/Severe assignment without fabricating a threshold not given in the article.
article.Age_Median: Methods reports two subgroup means, not one overall figure: 'The mean age was 34.6 +/- 1.9 years old for the opiate group and 37.5 +/- 2.9 years old for the cocaine group.' Both fall within the 30-50 bracket, so '30-50' is used despite no single combined mean being stated.
article.PercentFem: Methods: 'Participants included 27 treatment-seeking opioid- and cocaine-dependent men (n = 23) and women (n = 4).' 4/27 x 100 = 14.8%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: '.' No race or ethnicity data are reported anywhere in the article.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: 'NonUS', inferred rather than explicitly stated in Methods. Co-author affiliation (e) is 'Healing Visions Institute for Addiction Recovery, Ltd., St. Kitts, West Indies,' and the Acknowledgments separately thank 'the staff of the Healing Visions Institute for Addiction Recovery, Ltd., St. Kitts, W.I.' -- the institution most plausibly hosting the 14-day inpatient treatment described in Methods. 'Holistic Counseling, Inc., Miami, Florida' is also thanked, but the university/home-institution affiliations (Miami, Toronto, Montreal, Baltimore) are separate from the treatment site. Flagged because the Methods paragraph itself never names a country.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: 0. Subjects were 'self-referred for inpatient detoxification' for an experimental, non-standard-of-care treatment, with exclusion of anyone with stroke, epilepsy, or axis I psychotic disorder histories -- a self-selected, screened volunteer sample rather than a recruitment strategy reflective of a general treatment-seeking population.
article.InterventionTherapy: 0. Beyond drug administration, the study describes structured psychiatric evaluations (SCID I/II), the Addiction Severity Index, and a Psychosocial Assessment -- these are assessment/measurement instruments, not a described therapy, counseling, integration, or preparation component structured around the ibogaine session itself. 'Holistic Counseling, Inc., Miami, Florida' is thanked in the Acknowledgments but its role in the study protocol is never described, so it was not counted as evidence of an intervention-embedded therapy component.
article.HarmsAssessed: 1, required to agree with SafetyReported = 'Y' (see AE rationale below).
article.IndigenousFramework: 0. The Abstract/Introduction describe ibogaine's traditional use by 'indigenous peoples' of western Africa 'to combat fatigue, hunger and thirst, and... as a sacrament in religious rituals' -- this is background on the plant medicine's traditional origin, not integration of an Indigenous framework, knowledge system, or practice into this study's protocol. Matches the codebook's explicit 'traditional origin in passing is not integration' example.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: 1. Whole-blood pharmacokinetic levels of ibogaine and its metabolite noribogaine (FIGURE 1, GC/MS assay) are a central reported physiological/biological measure of this study, distinct from the baseline-only ECG/lab screening used for eligibility.
article.ReductionMeasured: 0. The study measures craving intensity (captured under BehaviorChangeMeasured) via the HCQN-29/CCQN-45, not a distinct partial-use-reduction or harm-reduction endpoint; no drug-use quantity/frequency outcome is reported (participants were inpatient throughout the assessed period).
article.CessationMeasured: 0. No abstinence or cessation rate is reported; the 1-month follow-up assessed self-reported craving only ('subjects' responses indicated that they still experienced diminished craving... (data not shown)'), not abstinence status.
article.RelapseMeasured: 0. Discussion explicitly places relapse tracking in future work, not this study: 'Future research efforts will be aimed at determining an association between CYP2D6 metabolizer status, depressive symptoms, drug craving, and relapse rates.'
article.Followup in months: 1. Longest reported follow-up is the self-report battery administered 'at one month following discharge from the treatment program' (Methods), i.e., measured from end of treatment.
article.SafetyReported: 'Y'. Methods states an aim was 'to determine the safety and effectiveness of ibogaine,' and Results states explicitly: 'Ibogaine was well tolerated by both opiate- and cocaine-dependent subjects, in agreement with our previous findings.' This is a brief but explicit safety statement, judged sufficient to clear the SafetyReported gate even though it is far less detailed than a dedicated AE table (the cited companion paper, ref 4, appears to carry the fuller safety analysis).
article.AnyAEReported: 'N'. The single safety statement in the article ('well tolerated... in agreement with our previous findings') is a positive tolerability claim with no adverse event of any kind named, counted, or described anywhere in the text. Treated as equivalent to an explicit no-AEs-occurred statement per the three-state framework, rather than 'AEs reported but not counted', since no specific AE is ever named.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: 0, consistent with AnyAEReported = 'N' (no AE of any kind was named).
article.AE_denominator: 27. All enrolled participants received ibogaine under the single-arm open-label protocol described in Methods; no separate 'safety population' distinct from the 27 enrolled is defined.

config_proposal.note: The selected primary craving statistic (HCQN-29 Intention-to-Use, opiate group) is an omnibus repeated-measures F with 3 numerator df across a 4-level within-subjects time factor, from a single-arm design with no comparator. Per the codebook, multi-df F statistics and within-subjects designs without a between-groups comparison are not convertible to Hedges' g and are marked excluded, to be routed to Tier 2 instead.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Single-arm open-label ibogaine trial with no control group. All 5 HCQN-29 opiate-craving subscales (TABLE 2, all p<=.0001) and 3 of 5 CCQN-45 cocaine-craving subscales (TABLE 3) showed statistically significant pre-to-post reductions, and BDI depression scores also decreased significantly across the study (F(3,18)=9.59, p=.0005, TABLE 1) -- a consistently positive pre/post direction across every reported outcome family, with no comparator arm to benchmark against.
